text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Terrorists" kill 33 villagers in Ksar el Boukhari area, south of Algiers, at the weekend. Among the dead were 14 women and four girls. The attack appears aimed at punishing a dissident gang through killing their families in the area. Seven bodies of civilians slaughtered by "terrorists" were found a day earlier in the same area. The same day, residents also found the body of a peasant, who was abducted, tortured and decapitated by "terrorists".
- "Terrorists" kidnapped 21 girls from Ksar el Boukhari area after the massacre of 33 villagers there. Eleven more civilians were killed in two hamlets in the same area.
- Drought scorched 65 percent of Algeria's cereal producing areas.
- The government earmarked 3.5 billion dinars ($62.5 million) for drought-stricken farmers who had paid an insurance policy.
- Drought cuts Algeria's grain harvest to 1.05 million tonnes for the 1996/1997 season from 4.9 million tonnes the previous season.
